description: Keep budget lines whose spent is 6.0 or more, including lines at exactly 6.0.

d.request: For each distinct event status, return the status value, the average of (budget.amount - budget.spent) for budget lines with budget.spent >= 6.0 that match to an event, the count of such matching budget lines, with null/missing values excluded from the average calculation.
d.sql: SELECT event.status, AVG(budget.amount - budget.spent) as avg_remaining, COUNT(*) as matching_budget_lines FROM budget JOIN event ON budget.link_to_event = event.event_id WHERE budget.spent >= 6.0 GROUP BY event.status

a.request: Linking each budget line to its event (`event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, exact text match; lines without a matching event are dropped), and considering only lines whose `spent` is at least 6.0, show for each event `status`: the status, the average of `amount` minus `spent` (ignoring missing values; blank if there are none), and the number of such budget lines. Leave the results unrounded.
a.sql: SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) as avg_remaining, COUNT(*) as num_budget_lines FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.spent >= 6.0 GROUP BY e.status

b.request: Group by event.status and report for each status: the status value, the average of (amount - spent) for budget lines where spent >= 6.0 that join to events by exact event_id match (excluding nulls from the average; blank if no such lines exist), and the count of budget lines, with all values unrounded.
b.sql: SELECT e.status, AVG(CASE WHEN b.spent >= 6.0 THEN (b.amount - b.spent) ELSE NULL END), COUNT(b.budget_id) FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON e.event_id = b.link_to_event GROUP BY e.status
b.raw: Group by event.status and report for each status: the status value, the average of (amount - spent) for budget lines where spent >= 6.0 that join to events by exact event_id match (excluding nulls from the average; blank if no such lines exist), and the count of budget lines, with all values unrounded.

c.request: Linking each budget line to its event (`event.event_id` = `budget.link_to_event`, exact text match; lines without a matching event are dropped), and using 6.0 as the cutoff on `spent` so that only the higher-spending budget lines are considered, show for each event `status`: the status, the average of `amount` minus `spent` (ignoring missing values; blank if there are none), and the number of such budget lines. Leave the results unrounded. Keep budget lines whose spent is 6.0 or more, including lines at exactly 6.0.
c.sql: SELECT e.status, AVG(b.amount - b.spent) AS avg_remaining, COUNT(*) AS budget_line_count FROM budget b INNER JOIN event e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE b.spent >= 6.0 GROUP BY e.status
